However, these alternative fuels have higher MFSPs than conventional diesel, ranging from 8% to 173%, with the exception of biocrude from sewage sludge via HTL, which has a lower MFSP than diesel. 18 In general, although e-fuel pathways have a good emission reduction ratio (84–98%), they still require higher MFSPs because these technologies are still in the early stages of development (e.g., e-MeOH and e--ammonia) with a low TRL of 3. RD and biocrude from sewage sludge via HTL pathways have competitive emission reductions and lower MFSPs. Note that waste feedstocks may have limited capacity, and therefore they may be unable to produce enough alternative fuel (see Figure 2-10).
